divisions.question: That this bill be now read a second time. That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: “while not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House expresses its concern that the Government’s decisions reflected in this bill have been made without consultation with business or other interested groups and calls on the Government to support reference of this bill and the Excise Legislation Amendment (Condensate) Bill 2008 to the Senate Economics Committee for inquiry so as to permit consultation with those with practical expertise and responsibility in this vital industry”. That the question be now put.
That these bills be now read a second time. That the amendment ( **Senator Xenophon’s** ) be agreed to.
That the motion ( **Senator Faulkner’s** ), as amended, be agreed to.
That the House of Representatives be requested to make the following amendments: That the requests ( **Senator Conroy’s** ) be agreed to.
That these bills be now read a third time.

speeches.speaker: John Faulkner
speeches.brief: The bills were introduced together, with a motion to proceed without formalities and be read a first time, which was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: John Faulkner
speeches.brief: The speech introduced bills to implement the Montreal Convention for international air carrier liability, strengthen Customs border enforcement and search powers, modernise customs procedures, define tobacco content for duty, and amend the Export Market Development Grants scheme. Key changes include removing the air liability cap with claims up to 100,000 SDR (about A$172,000), and raising the EMDG maximum grant to $200,000, the turnover limit to $50 million, and lowering the expenditure threshold to $10,000.

speeches.speaker: Chris Ellison
speeches.brief: The opposition moved to refer several government bills to Senate committees for extended inquiry, arguing they required careful scrutiny and were not election policies. The government accused the opposition of economic vandalism, claiming the delays would cost up to $284 million and undermine the budget surplus strategy.
The debate resumed on the luxury car tax bills, with an amendment moved by Senators Bartlett and Nettle to require passage by 24 June 2008 and to omit paragraph (2) of the motion.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the opposition is delaying eight bills through Senate committee referrals without proper justification, including the Same-Sex Relationships (Superannuation) Bill 2008 and the Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Political Donations and Other Measures) Bill 2008. The speaker urged the opposition to support the same‑sex superannuation bill by 1 July, and to pass electoral reforms lowering the donation disclosure threshold to $1,000, banning overseas and anonymous donations, and preventing parties from profiting from public funding.

speeches.speaker: Kerry O'Brien
speeches.brief: The report of the Standing Committee on Economics on the Excise Legislation Amendment (Condensate) Bill 2008, the Excise Tariff Amendment (Condensate) Bill 2008 and related matters was presented and ordered to be printed.

speeches.speaker: David Johnston
speeches.brief: The legislation removes the 1977 crude-oil excise exemption for condensate produced from the North West Shelf and onshore fields, raising an estimated $2.5 billion over the forward estimates. Supporters argued the mature, highly profitable ventures no longer needed the subsidy, while opponents condemned the unannounced change as a tax grab that would be passed on to Western Australian households and damage Australia’s sovereign-risk reputation.

speeches.speaker: Gary Humphries
speeches.brief: The government argued that applying crude oil excise to condensate from the North West Shelf project would raise $2.5 billion and close a loophole, while the opposition countered that it was an unfair double tax, that Woodside claimed they would have paid $8 billion less under PRRT, and that the government did no modelling on potential price increases for domestic gas and electricity in Western Australia.
